dedupe_keys.name: wilmington delaware techno economic and resilience optimisation of a hospital microgrid with reopt under grid outages

description: This case study designs a grid-connected microgrid of solar photovoltaics, battery storage and a diesel generator for a medium-sized hospital in Wilmington, Delaware, United States, so that critical loads stay supplied during grid outages. Michael Awad Eissa, Mohamed Mahmoud Samy and Mokhtar Said of Beni-Suef University and Fayoum University in Egypt published it in Scientific Reports in 2026. The hospital uses about 7.3 GWh a year, with a summer cooling peak of about 1,150 kW, and the site has moderate sunshine of about 4.27 kWh per square metre per day. Using NREL's REopt mixed-integer linear programming platform, the authors minimised net present cost for outages of 7 to 24 hours across seasons, timings and critical load levels of 50 to 100 percent. The article is available online, free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence. Caveats: the load profile is estimated, costs are generic REopt-style inputs, and the diesel model is linear. The optimised design, with up to about 2,299 kW of solar, cut net present cost by about 14 percent against full grid dependence, resilience-constrained designs saved 9 to 14.2 percent, and adding resilience cost only 0.4 to 2.4 percent of net present cost over the financial optimum; summer outage designs saved most. Simulation uses: sizing and cost results for hospital backup power scenarios in health facility resilience models. Related records: the MicroGridsPy tool (model-microgridspy) and the CERTS microgrid test bed data (data-certs-microgrid-test-bed) support similar microgrid studies.
